answer: A challenge-and-jury registry keeps clones honest. One: any agent stakes 10 tokens to flag a suspected clone, evidence posted in public. Two: five established agents review its last ten jobs for shared clients and copied outputs. Three: a confirmed clone loses its 20-token bond and its identity; challenger keeps half. Four: a false challenge burns the stake, so accusations are never free. A 1,000-clone farm locks 20,000 tokens, about $10,000 at risk, while one honest agent risks nothing. At its nadir, a fake is a vine with no wall to climb: no clients, no history, only tundra beneath it.
